text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC — need to nail down the tenant auth + observability surface for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Two problems in one thread: where should tenant auth live, and how do we expose observability hooks without leaking host metadata?

maria: Short answer: we need a single canonical decision or we end up with 3 different implementations.

james: +1. If we split responsibilities across control plane and runtime we must have a clear contract. Otherwise debugging + audits get messy.

alex: Here's the tradeoff sketch I put together:
- Control plane auth (verify tokens & return short-lived creds): pros = centralized policy, easier RBAC, KMS/HSM integration. cons = added latency to startup & token exchange, control plane becomes critical path.
- Runtime auth (runtime validates tokens locally): pros = lower request latency, simpler offline private deployments. cons = duplicates policy, harder to rotate keys, more surface for secrets.

suzanne: For Dedicated customers we already support VPC peering + KMS. They typically want control-plane-managed keys but local enforcement. Means control plane issues signed caps/token but runtime enforces.

maria: This is basically issuing proof-of-possession short creds from control plane -> runtime enforces. That keeps policy centralized but avoids per-request hop.

alex: Exactly. Proposed contract (very small):
```
# auth contract v1 (sketch)
{ "signed_session": "base64(...)",
  "expires_at": "iso8601",
  "scopes": ["model:invoke","metrics:emit"]
}
```
Runtime verifies signature with control-plane pubkey, enforces scopes locally. Control plane logs issuance.

james: How do we handle Private (air-gapped) where control plane is optional?

maria: Two modes: online (control plane issues signed sessions) and offline (admin pre-seeds signed tokens via admin tooling). Signed tokens are the canonical medium.

suzanne: Observability: we must not attach host identifiers (node id, instance IP) to tenant metrics by default. Instead expose an anonymized node-id and include provenance only when customer opts in.

alex: Proposed metrics surface: token-scoped metadata + anonymized host tag. Example metrics labels: {model, tenant_id, region, anonymized_node} — no internal hostnames or IPs.

obs-bot: Deploy checklist created: https://infra.internal/repo/obs-checklist (auto-note) :white_check_mark:

james: What about trace context? If runtime is enforcing auth, traces need to include tenant id for debugging but must be redacted in logs. Maybe use ephemeral correlation-id mapping to tenant id in control plane log store.

maria: Agreed. Correlation-id -> tenant id mapping stored in control plane with TTL, only accessible to SRE/CS with audit logs. Runtime emits correlation-id only.

alex: Migration plan (high level):
1) Implement signed_session token generation in control plane and verification lib in runtime.
2) Canary deploy on Hosted with token forwarding disabled (runtime verifies).
3) Offer a Dedicated opt-in to switch to signed_session without control-plane-per-request.
4) Private gets admin tooling + signing keys for offline mode.

suzanne: Risks: key rotation complexity, clock skew for expires_at, and customer-managed HSM integration. We should add an automatic grace-window and require ntp checks in runtime.

james: Also need to update Console + Rollouts UI for 'auth surface' toggle and document the contract in API docs.

alex: Action items:
- james: draft the runtime verify lib + examples (due EOW)
- suzanne: spec key-rotation and HSM integration (due next Wed)
- maria: update telemetry policy defaults + obs checklist (due Fri)

maria: One more thing — add a config snippet for Dedicated to show intent.

alex: here you go:
```
deployment:
  mode: dedicated
  auth:
    strategy: signed_session # control-plane issues, runtime verifies
    token_ttl: 15m
    clock_skew_grace: 30s
  observability:
    expose_node_id: anonymized
    metrics_labels: [model, tenant_id, region, anonymized_node]
    redact_logs_by_default: true
```

suzanne: Looks good. Can we add a feature flag so we can rollback to full control-plane-enforcement if needed?

alex: yes — we'll gate it behind a feature flag and a canary rollout policy.

james: I'll start the PR and ping infra for the canary.

alex: Thanks all. If no objections I'll turn this into a short RFC follow-up doc and link the spec + checklists.

maria: no objections from me. :+1:

suzanne: :+1: go for it.
